item.title: There are these two kinds of assemblies, bhikkhus. What two? A superficial assembly and a profound assembly. And, bhikkhus, what is a superficial assembly? Here,…
item.description:
There are these two kinds of assemblies, bhikkhus. What two? A superficial assembly and a profound assembly. And, bhikkhus, what is a superficial assembly? Here, bhikkhus, in whatever assembly there are bhikkhus who are restless, arrogant, talkative, garrulous, unmindful, not clearly comprehending, unconcentrated, with distracted minds and loose faculties. This, bhikkhus, is called a superficial assembly. And, bhikkhus, what is a profound assembly? Here, bhikkhus, in whatever assembly there are bhikkhus who are not restless, not arrogant, not agitated, not talkative, not garrulous, mindful, clearly comprehending, concentrated, with unified minds and guarded faculties. This, bhikkhus, is called a profound assembly.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 2.42

item.title: Bhikkhus, just as an oil lamp burns dependent on oil and a wick. From time to time a man pours in oil and adjusts the…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, just as an oil lamp burns dependent on oil and a wick. From time to time a man pours in oil and adjusts the wick. Bhikkhus, that oil lamp, being nourished, being supplied, would burn for a long time. So too, bhikkhus, one who lives seeing gratification in things that can be fettered, craving increases. With craving as condition, clinging arises ... Thus is the origination of this whole mass of suffering. Bhikkhus, just as an oil lamp burns dependent on oil and a wick. Then a man does not pour in oil from time to time and does not adjust the wick. Thus, bhikkhus, that oil lamp, as its former fuel is consumed and no other fuel is supplied, being not nourished, would be extinguished. So too, bhikkhus, one who lives seeing danger in things that can be fettered, craving ceases. With the cessation of craving, clinging ceases ... Thus is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.54

item.title: Who here, having abandoned sensual pleasures, Has gone forth from home to homelessness, Having destroyed both sensual desire and existence, That one I call a…
item.description:
Who here, having abandoned sensual pleasures,
Has gone forth from home to homelessness,
Having destroyed both sensual desire and existence,
That one I call a brahmin.

Who here, having abandoned craving,
Has gone forth from home to homelessness,
Having destroyed both craving and existence,
That one I call a brahmin.

Who has abandoned the human yoke
And crossed beyond the divine yoke,
Who is free from all bonds,
Released from bondage,
That one I call a brahmin.

Who has abandoned pleasure and displeasure,
Who is cool, without attachments,
Who has conquered all worlds,
That heroic one,
That one I call a brahmin.

Who knows fully the passing away and rebirth
Of beings in all their forms,
Who is unattached, well-gone, enlightened,
Attained the supreme enlightenment,
That one I call a brahmin.

Whose destination is unknown
To devas, spirits, or humans,
Who is taintless, an Arahant,
That one I call a brahmin.

Who has no clinging to the past, future, or present,
Who is without attachment, without possession,
That one I call a brahmin.

Who is the bull of a man, the hero,
The great sage, the conqueror,
The passionless, the purified, the awakened,
That one I call a brahmin.

Who knows his former lives,
Who sees the good and bad destinations,
Who has reached the end of birth,
That one I call a brahmin.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 98 – Vāseṭṭhasutta

item.title: Elder Vimala: Avoid evil friends, associate with the noble ones. Follow their advice, incline toward unshakable happiness. Like climbing a small plank on the ocean,…
item.description:
Elder Vimala:

Avoid evil friends, associate with the noble ones.
Follow their advice, incline toward unshakable happiness.

Like climbing a small plank on the ocean, one sinks;
So too, one of good conduct sinks when associating with others.
Therefore avoid the lazy, the indolent.

Live near the noble ones, the secluded, the energetic,
Meditative, always striving, the wise and clear-sighted.

From: Theragāthā 3.16

item.title: Bhikkhus, if anyone were to say: 'A complete snare of Māra,' he would rightly say that of women. Truly, 'a complete snare of Māra' —…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, if anyone were to say: 'A complete snare of Māra,' he would rightly say that of women. Truly, 'a complete snare of Māra' — that is what women are.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.55

item.title: Friends, what is pursuit of the past? 'My eye in the past was such and such, forms were such and such, and consciousness there was…
item.description:
Friends, what is pursuit of the past? 'My eye in the past was such and such, forms were such and such, and consciousness there was bound by desire and craving.' Because consciousness is bound by desire and craving, he delights in that. Delighting in that, he pursues the past. 'My ear in the past was such and such, sounds were such and such... My nose in the past was such and such, odors were such and such... My tongue in the past was such and such, flavors were such and such... My mind in the past was such and such, mental objects were such and such, and consciousness there was bound by desire and craving.' Because consciousness is bound by desire and craving, he delights in that. Delighting in that, he pursues the past. Thus, friends, is pursuit of the past.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 133 – Mahākaccānabhaddekarattasutta

item.title: The Blessed One: From these causes, desire and ill-will arise; From them arise liking and disliking, and fear. From them arise the thoughts of the…
item.description:
The Blessed One:
From these causes, desire and ill-will arise;
From them arise liking and disliking, and fear.
From them arise the thoughts of the mind.
Like children releasing a crow, they go.

The identification with a self arises from affection,
Like a banyan tree from its trunk.
The manifold bonds of sensual pleasures are spread,
Like a maluva creeper in the forest.

Those who know whence it arises
Remove its root. They cross this flood,
So hard to cross, not crossed before,
And do not come to renewed existence.

From: Sutta Nipāta 2.5

item.title: Ambattha, just as a young partridge can sing freely in its nest. Ambattha, Kapilavatthu belongs to the Sakya clan. It is not fitting for Ambattha…
item.description:
Ambattha, just as a young partridge can sing freely in its nest. Ambattha, Kapilavatthu belongs to the Sakya clan. It is not fitting for Ambattha to be displeased over such a trivial matter.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 3 – Ambaṭṭhasutta

item.title: How, Ānanda, is it that four foundations of mindfulness, when developed and cultivated, perfect the seven factors of enlightenment? Whenever, Ānanda, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating…
item.description:
How, Ānanda, is it that four foundations of mindfulness, when developed and cultivated, perfect the seven factors of enlightenment? Whenever, Ānanda, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body, his mindfulness is established; at that time, Ānanda, a bhikkhu is mindful, not forgetful. Whenever, Ānanda, a bhikkhu abides mindful, not forgetful, then the mindfulness enlightenment factor is aroused in that bhikkhu. Whenever, Ānanda, a bhikkhu develops the mindfulness enlightenment factor, then, through development, the mindfulness enlightenment factor comes to fulfillment. Abiding thus mindful, he wisely investigates, examines, and contemplates that Dhamma.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 54.13

item.title: Bhikkhus, I say that almsfood is of two kinds: to be used and not to be used — thus it has been said. For what…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, I say that almsfood is of two kinds: to be used and not to be used — thus it has been said. For what reason is it said? Here, if one knows of a certain almsfood: 'This almsfood, when I use it, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decrease' — then such almsfood should not be used. Here, if one knows of a certain almsfood: 'This almsfood, when I use it, unwholesome states decrease and wholesome states increase' — then such almsfood should be used.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.54
